catering-pricing-guide.html.text:
Catering Quote Calculator · guide

How to price catering per person, and what a minimum guest count is for

Short answer: price = total cost ÷ (1 − margin − overhead), divided by guests. The part that catches caterers is that only some costs grow with headcount, so a flat per-head price quietly loses money on small events.

Sort every cost into three kinds

  • Per guest: food, plates, cutlery, napkins. Add a waste allowance (5% is a common start) because you always cook or buy more than is eaten.
  • Per event: van and fuel, chafing dishes, linen rental, permits. They do not change with the guest count.
  • Staff hours: cooks, servers, setup. Add payroll burden (taxes and workers' comp, 10 to 15 percent is typical) and remember setup and breakdown hours count.

Why price per head falls as the event grows

With $1,400 of fixed cost and $10 of food per guest, 30 guests cost $56.67 per head and 120 guests cost $21.67. The calculator prints this tier table so you can quote different headcounts without redoing the sheet.

Find the minimum guest count

Take the per-guest price you will actually quote, subtract overhead and the per-guest cost, and divide the fixed costs by what is left. That is the break-even headcount. Put a minimum at or above it in the contract, with the price per head for fewer guests stated.

Deposits and tax

A deposit of half the quote at booking is common because ingredients and staff are committed early. Sales tax, service charges and gratuity are usually shown on separate lines; whether they apply, and who keeps them, depends on your state, so check the local rule instead of assuming.

node cli.mjs quote event.csv --guests 60 --price 28

Common questions

How much should a caterer charge per person?

Enough that cost divided by one minus your margin and overhead share gives the price. With a 30% margin and 10% overhead that is cost divided by 0.6, so a $26 per guest cost needs a price near $43. The calculator does this from your own lines.

What is a minimum guest count for?

Staff, rentals and fuel cost the same whether 40 or 60 people come, so below a certain headcount the event loses money. The break-even guest count is where the price you quoted covers those fixed costs, and the minimum should sit at or above it.

What food cost percentage should a caterer target?

Many caterers aim for food at roughly 25 to 35 percent of the quote and staff at a similar level, but menus differ widely. The tool warns at 35 percent for each and the levels are yours to change.

No warranty. This guide and the tool are free and as-is, without warranty of any kind. Not financial, tax, legal or food-safety advice; the levels quoted are rules of thumb. Licensing, insurance, health-code and sales-tax rules for catering vary by place.

CATERING QUOTE CALCULATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

What should this catering job cost per guest — and how few guests can you take?

Paste your costs for one event — food per guest, staff hours, rentals, fuel — and see the per-guest price that delivers your margin, food and labor as a share of the quote, the deposit and the guest count below which you lose money.

Nothing is uploaded and no supplier or accounting tool is contacted. The text box is analysed in this browser and never leaves your device. The 35% food and labor warning levels, 30% margin and 10% overhead are common rules of thumb, not a standard, and you can change every one.

Prefer a CLI, or want to quote from a script?

Same logic, zero dependencies, one command — reads a file or stdin:

node cli.mjs quote event.csv --guests 60
cat event.csv | node cli.mjs quote - --guests 60 --margin 30
node cli.mjs quote event.csv --guests 60 --price 28 --json --fail-on error

Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. Exit code 1 on a losing price, so a script can refuse to send it. More: How to price catering per person, and what a minimum guest count is for.

What's recognised

InputHandling

Warning levels, margin and overhead are rules of thumb; sales tax and gratuity are shown separately and never counted as revenue; supplier price changes, no-shows below a guarantee and venue rules are not modelled.

Common questions

Does this connect to a POS or accounting system?

No. It reads the cost lines you paste and never contacts Square, Toast, QuickBooks or any supplier. Every figure is arithmetic on the lines you gave it, so nothing here leaves your device.

How is the per-guest price calculated?

Total cost divided by (1 minus your target margin minus your overhead share), then divided by the guest count. Per-guest lines scale with the guests, flat and staff lines do not, which is why a bigger event costs less per head.

What are the three line types?

guest is a cost per person (food, plates), with a waste allowance added; flat is a cost for the whole event (van, rentals, permits); staff-hour is total staff hours times the hourly rate, with a payroll-burden allowance added.

What is the break-even guest count?

The number of guests at which the price you name covers the fixed costs after overhead. Below it the event loses money, so it is the number to put in a minimum-guest clause.

Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The browser page runs on the text in your own browser and never sends it anywhere. The CLI reads a local file or stdin and makes no network call.
